title: Pass existing buffers to stream consumers
goal: Adapt borrowed memory, segmented bytes or encoded text to a Stream reader without first flattening the whole input.

selectionNotes: Keep borrowed bytes/chars valid and unchanged until every stream read finishes. WritableMemoryStream has fixed capacity.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses .NET 11 library APIs; the .NET 10 code is a comparison, not a catalogue route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 sample with the .NET 11 SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical net11.0 project selects the .NET 11 default C# 15 language mode.

prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0. Include the imports stated in the recipe.
constraints: Adapters do not transfer ownership or extend a pool/pipe buffer’s valid lifetime. Finish and dispose the reader/stream before returning memory to a pool or advancing a PipeReader; do not mutate it concurrently. ReadOnly means the stream cannot write, not that the original owner cannot change bytes. WritableMemoryStream writes into the supplied slice and cannot grow. StringStream needs an explicit Encoding and can allocate encoding working storage; avoiding a whole-input byte array is not a zero-allocation promise. Its ReadOnlyMemory<char> source must also remain valid. Encoding fallback/BOM detection are independent choices; this example uses UTF-8 and StreamReader’s ordinary BOM detection. Capability flags differ by adapter: inspect CanRead/CanWrite/CanSeek rather than assuming MemoryStream’s full contract.
stabilityLimitations: RC2 verification; GA reconciliation remains pending.
